145:// nestedInvocation reports whether a hook payload came from a Pi process that has
146:// no session of its own, in which case the payload must not be resolved against
147:// the per-repo session-ID cache.
148://
149:// Pi has no subagent events; subagents come from an extension (see Pi's
150:// `subagent/` example) that spawns `pi --mode json -p --no-session` with cwd set to
151:// the project directory. Pi auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/*/index.ts`
152:// there, so the child loads Entire's own extension and fires these hooks too. With
153:// --no-session it reports no session file, so sessionID is empty — and the cache is
154:// a single per-repo file, so falling back to it handed the child its *parent's*
155:// session ID. The nested turn then overwrote the parent's last prompt with the
156:// subagent's internal task text and opened a new turn mid-flight, so the
157:// checkpoint's title and turn-scoped windows described the subagent, not the user.
158://
159:// Requiring a session file keeps the legitimate fallback — a session file whose
160:// name carries no parseable ID — while making sessionless invocations a clean
161:// no-op. Nothing is lost for agent_end either: captureTranscript returns "" without
162:// a session file, so such an event could only ever fail downstream with "transcript
163:// file not specified".
164://
165:// An explicit payload session_id is always honoured; only the cache is distrusted.
